extracted.intended_audience: federal agency managers and procurement/ADP officials responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-76 (ADP program managers, agency heads, contracting officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for executive agencies on when and how to rely on commercial sources for automatic data processing (ADP) requirements, including planning, acquisition, cost-comparison, exceptions, termination, and administrative responsibilities under OMB Circular A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy preference for commercial ADP services
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with the Government's general policy of reliance on the private sector, agencies will obtain ADP services from competitive commercial sources in preference to direct operation of in-house activities, except as provided in paragraph 5 of Circular No. A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct procurement of services is the preferred alternative; agencies retain in-house expertise to prepare service performance specifications and to monitor contractor performance. Government ADP operations that cannot be justified under Circular A-76 shall be terminated in a planned and appropriate manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability / scope to general-purpose ADP activities
rubrics_metrics.description: This Transmittal Memorandum is applicable to all general purpose data processing activities operated and managed by executive agencies that provide services that are obtainable from a private source, as defined in Circular No. A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular applies to Government commercial or industrial activities which provide for Government use a product or service obtainable from private sources. It excludes Government-owned contractor-operated activities and has specific exceptions (see exclusions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances permitting Government provision (exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government commercial or industrial activity may be authorized only under one or more conditions: (a) procurement from a commercial source would disrupt or materially delay an agency's program; (b) necessary for combat support, retraining, or mobilization readiness; (c) a satisfactory commercial source is not available in time; (d) the product or service is available from another Federal agency; (e) procurement from commercial source will result in higher cost to the Government (comparative cost analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified status or relation to an agency program alone is not an adequate reason for exception, but a documented review may establish disruption. Also, do not apply where inconsistent with treaties or international agreements (paragraph 4.f.).

rubrics_metrics.name: New starts: definition and approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new start' (newly established activity or significant re-activation/expansion/modernization) must not be initiated until possibilities of obtaining the product/service from commercial sources have been explored and it is approved by the agency head or equivalent on the basis of factual justification under the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold dollar amounts define new starts (see Circular); a new start ordinarily should not be approved for comparative-cost reasons unless government costs are at least 10 percent less than commercial costs, though 10% is not fixed and may vary with circumstances (larger for big capital investments or obsolescence risk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-comparison requirement and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost studies to determine whether a commercial ADP activity can be justified on the basis of cost should be limited to situations where there is reason to assume in-house costs will be significantly less than competitive commercial prices. Commercial sources should be relied upon without delay for products/services estimated to cost the Government less than $50,000 per year unless there is reason to suspect unreasonable commercial prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost studies are required for many cases (including when contract terms cause the Government to finance > $50,000 for facilities) and when there is reason to believe savings are possible; do not run cost studies where in-house or commercial procurement is otherwise clearly justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost study elements — commercial cost components
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of obtaining products or services from commercial sources should include amounts paid directly to suppliers, transportation charges, and expenses of preparing bid invitations, evaluating bids, and negotiating, awarding, and managing contracts; costs of materials furnished by the Government to contractors; appropriate charges for Government-owned equipment/facilities used by contractors; and costs due to incentive or premium contract provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also include costs such as standby costs if discontinuance of Government activity places facilities on standby, and increased retirement costs if discontinuance causes premature retirements. Commercial cost estimates must be documented and organized for equitable comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost study elements — Government cost components
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of obtaining products or services from Government activities should include all costs which would be incurred by the Government and would not be incurred if the product or service were obtained commercially — computed as incremental/additional costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly include: (1) personal services and benefits (full cost of retirement calculated on a normal cost basis, Social Security where applicable, insurance, allowances, termination costs); (2) materials, supplies, utilities and logistics; (3) maintenance and repair; (4) damage/loss/insurance; (5) Federal taxes (corporate income and similar revenues lost to Treasury if procured commercially); (6) depreciation with recognition of residual/salvage; (7) interest computed on long-term Treasury yields with straight-line reduction; (8) indirect costs (management, budgeting, legal, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing cost differential for new starts
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost differential favoring reliance on commercial sources should reflect the possibility of early obsolescence and the uncertainty of ADP requirements; Circular A-76 specifies that this differential should normally be at least 10% for any new start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ADP activities this differential can be substantially more than 10% and should be set appropriately for the degree of risk and uncertainty in each cost study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of valid commercial cost figure
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of a valid commercial cost figure generally requires solicitation of competitive bids for the required services; the Government and commercial cost estimates must be based on equivalent services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial firms have indicated willingness to provide cost/price proposals if assured of objective cost studies. Particular attention should be given to ensuring equivalence of service requirements and fair-market valuation of equipment/facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressing ADP requirements in terms of services
rubrics_metrics.description: Government ADP requirements normally will be expressed in terms of the services to be performed, rather than the equipment and software to be used in performing these services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements of requirements should allow the contractor maximum flexibility in the type of equipment and personnel used, as long as satisfactory services are provided. This supports competition and contractor innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSA delegation requests must reference A-76 review
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency requests to the General Services Administration for delegation of procurement authority for acquisition of ADP equipment to be operated by the agency will include a specific statement indicating that the proposed acquisition has been reviewed and approved under the provisions of Circular No. A-76, or an explanation of why the Circular does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures acquisitions that effectively procure services or result in in-house operation are consistent with A-76 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning and management requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will initiate actions to ensure full implementation of the policy, including review/revision of agency instructions, maximum emphasis on 'new starts' review, preparation of a multiyear ADP plan (to be included in the Spring ADP Plan to OMB), and development of a program outline with milestones and specific targets for submission to OMB within 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, agencies should set goals and make use of Management by Objective (MBO) methodology to increase reliance on the private sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and transition planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Current agency ADP operations that cannot be justified shall be terminated in a planned and appropriate manner. Reviews should determine whether government performance is justified and, when activities are to be terminated or reduced, the action must be carefully planned to ensure transition without disruption of vital services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning should include phased reduction to facilitate reassignment and reduction by attrition, reasonable consideration for displaced employees, careful coordination of contract services, and overlap periods when necessary to avoid mission disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory and review schedule of commercial/industrial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will compile and maintain an inventory of its commercial or industrial activities having an annual output costing $50,000 or more or a capital investment of $25,000 or more; the inventory should include capital investment, annual payments, and the basis upon which the activity is being continued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities should be reviewed (including previously approved new starts in operation at least 18 months) and reviews documented; initial inventories and reviews had specified deadlines in the Circular and follow-up reviews should be scheduled at least once every three years unless exempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration / implementation responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency is responsible for making the provisions effective by issuing implementing instructions and by providing adequate management support and procedures for review and follow-up; overall responsibility should be assigned to a senior official reporting directly to the agency head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of implementing instructions must be furnished to the Bureau of the Budget (now OMB). If legislation is needed agencies should prepare proposals in accordance with Bureau/OMB procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability exclusions and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular A-76 will not be used as authority to enter contracts if such authority does not otherwise exist, nor to justify departure from laws/regulations (including Civil Service rules) or to avoid established salary/personnel limitations; it does not apply to managerial advisory services, products/services provided to the public, or products/services obtained from other Federal agencies; should not be applied where inconsistent with treaties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must retain essential management functions (selection, direction, assignment, evaluation) and exercise caution in interpreting exemptions (e.g., 'professional staff' wording was narrowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-comparison methodology simplifications
rubrics_metrics.description: For economy and simplicity, generally agreed costs that would tend to be the same under either alternative need not be measured and included in comparative cost analyses (for example, bid and award costs and operating costs under lease-purchase alternatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the incremental-cost method to compute the realistic additional cost to the Government under each alternative; do not include mutual costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of depreciation and interest in cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate recognition should be given to estimated residual or salvage values of facilities or equipment when computing depreciation; interest for any new/additional capital should be computed based on the average rate of yield for long-term Treasury bonds with reduction in the capital investment to which interest is applied over the asset's life on a straight-line basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accelerated depreciation rates permitted by the IRS will not be used; these rules provide a consistent basis for comparing government capital costs to commercial alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include indirect, standby, and retirement-cost consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons should include additional indirect costs (management, supervision, budgeting, accounting, personnel, legal and other services), costs of preparing/maintaining a facility as standby if discontinuance is expected, and increased retirement costs if discontinuance will cause premature retirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include these items can misrepresent the true cost of discontinuing Government activities; include them in the appropriate side of the comparative cost analysis.
